title: Small-batch Beta Runway & KPI Initiative Log
content:
Purpose:
This is the canonical small-batch beta runway plan and KPI initiative log for the Search Assistant feature (hosted + dedicated variants). Goal: validate production economics and quality at 1–5k daily active users in controlled cohorts before broad beta. This doc captures acceptance criteria, phased traffic plan, KPI targets, preflight checklist, staffing rota, and contingency playbook.

Scope:
- Incumbents: hosted API + Redwood Dedicated pool (GPU X1) for the same model family.
- Cohorts: 3 customer pilots (pilot A/B/C) + internal dogfood.
- Duration: 6 weeks of staged ramp, 2-week observation.
- Not included: on-prem private deploys for this run (separate track).

Executive summary (1–2 lines):
- Run a controlled small-batch beta to validate latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics. If KPIs hold at target, approve scale to open beta.

KPI targets (pass/fail thresholds):
- Latency (p95, end-to-end from request arrival to first token): <= 450ms (short prompts <= 256 tokens).
- Median latency (p50): <= 150ms.
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts): <= 0.5%.
- Token cost (effective, after batching and caching): <= $0.20 per 1k tokens for hosted, <= $0.12 per 1k tokens on Dedicated (target internal unit economics).
- Quality: automated eval similarity F1 >= 0.82 on the 120-item prompt set; manual raters >= 85% satisfactory responses.
- Availability during business hours (US-PST): 99.9% for pilot traffic.

Baseline metrics (from canary + perf tests):
- Current p95 observed (staging): 420ms avg, variability +80ms during synthetic burst.
- Error rate staging: 0.2% under 50 RPS sustained.
- Typical token mix: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64–256), 10% long (>256).
- Batch sizes: median effective batch = 6 requests in Dedicated tests.

Runway phases and traffic routing (dates are nominal):
- Phase 0 — Internal dogfood (week 0): 50 daily DAU, smoke-only; objective: validate logs, trace hooks, and KV caching.
- Phase 1 — Pilot alpha (week 1–2): 3 customers, up to 200 DAU each, total <= 600 DAU; routing: 90% to hosted, 10% to Dedicated for regression comparison.
- Phase 2 — Small-batch beta (week 3–4): expand to 1k DAU; routing: 75% hosted, 25% Dedicated; enable low-latency routing policy for high-value pilots.
- Phase 3 — Beta expansion (week 5–6): 3–5k DAU soft-open; routing: dynamic (policy by cost/latency); gated go/no-go at end of week 6.

Traffic shaping (operational knobs):
- Ramp steps: 5% -> 15% -> 35% -> 60% -> 100% per cohort, 24–48h between steps.
- Burst window policy: cap requests per second per customer (default 8 RPS, burst to 20 RPS with token bucket for 60s).
- Warm caches: pre-seed top 50 session prefixes for pilots to improve cache hit rate.

Acceptance criteria & go/no-go signals (automated):
- Primary green: p95 latency < target AND error rate < target for 48h rolling.
- Secondary green: token cost within target band for last 7 days AND no quality regression > 2% vs baseline eval set.
- Red flags (fail-fast): sustained p95 increase > 30% over baseline OR error spike > 1% OR manual raters report relevance drop > 5%.

Preflight checklist (owners assigned):
- API & SDK: verify version pinning and client timeouts (owner: Owen Patel).
- Model pin: confirm model hash and quantization artifact on both hosted and Dedicated (owner: Lena García).
- Console dashboards: per-route latency, token cost, per-customer SLI (owner: Marcus O'Neill).
- Tracing: request-id propagation end-to-end and sampling set to 100% for pilot traffic (owner: Aisha Rahman).
- Logging: ensure prompt redaction, PII rules active, request-level cost tagging (owner: Maya Chen).
- Canary synthetic: run 3-hour synthetic spike with mixed prompt mix, record p50/p95, error rates (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Rollback plan: traffic cut by 50% and fallback to smaller model variant within 10 minutes (owner: platform-engineering).

Staffing and on-call rota (week-of-launch):
- Launch day core team (09:00–21:00 PST): Product Ops (Maya), Oncall SRE (Marcus), Serving runtime lead (Lena), Solutions Eng (Owen).
- Night watch (21:00–09:00 PST): SRE & infra pager; product ops on standby for escalations.
- Escalation matrix: pager -> SRE -> Serving runtime -> Platform Eng -> CTO on-call.

Monitoring & data capture (what we store & where):
- Metrics: per-route request latency histograms, token counts, errors, batch sizes. Aggregated daily and 1m granularity.
- Traces: 100% for pilot traffic for first 72h, then 5% sampling. Stored in tracing cluster (linked_artifacts).
- Quality: save all prompts/responses (with PII redaction) to eval bucket and run nightly evals vs benchmark prompt set.

Contingency actions (playbook):
- If p95 spikes but error rate stable: reduce batch window to favor latency (config change) and limit new sessions for 15 minutes.
- If error rate increases: immediate traffic hold (stop new traffic ingress), notify pilots, failover traffic to fallback model variant.
- If quality regression: kill new rollout, revert model pin, and open eval triage (owner: Applied ML).
- If cost exceeds target: throttle non-key customers, enable higher quantization profile for low-priority routes.

Data & evaluation plan:
- Eval sets: 120 prompt QA set (public + synthetic), 30 adversarial prompts, 12 business-critical prompts per pilot.
- Nightly automated eval: compute similarity F1, hallucination rate, response length distribution.
- Weekly manual review: 10 random responses per pilot; 3 human raters.

Rollout timeline (milestones):
- Nov 11 (week 0): dogfood complete, dashboards validated.
- Nov 18 (week 1): pilot alpha start.
- Dec 2 (week 3): small-batch beta start.
- Dec 16 (week 5): beta expansion gating decision.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Data residency ask from Pilot B: need to confirm whether Dedicated pool in EU region is available for their dataset (owner: infra).
- Model variant parity: do embeddings/response tokens differ by quant profile? (owner: Applied ML).
- SLA uplift: do pilots need temporary enhanced SLA? pricing/contract check with GTM.

Next steps (immediate):
- Finalize pilot cohort list + contact points (owner: Maya) — due 2025-11-07.
- Schedule 3-hour synthetic canary (owner: eng-serving-runtime) — due 2025-11-09.
- Configure per-route dashboards and alerts (owner: Marcus) — due 2025-11-10.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately operational and checklist-heavy; please flag any missing owners or tooling gaps.
- If the cost modeling looks off, attach runbook numbers and we will re-run offline with Redwood Optimize outputs.

Hand-off checklist at end of run (what we will produce):
- Post-run KPI summary (p50/p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, batch stats).
- Quality review doc with manual rater notes.
- Recommendation: green/amber/red and suggested next step (open beta or additional optimizations).

Appendix (quick command fragments):
- To reduce batch window via API: POST /admin/runtime/config { "batch_window_ms":50 } (requires platform-engineering approval).
- To enable fallback model for route: PATCH /routes/{id}/policy { "fallback_model": "redwood-model-v1-small" }

-- end of log --
